record.text: How is European research trying to replace the traditional remedy for people bitten by poisonous snakes - the kind produced from the blood of animals repeatedly exposed to the poison - with proteins engineered in the laboratory instead?
record.reference_answer: Two projects pursue laboratory-made replacements for conventional antivenoms, which are derived from immunised animals (ADDovenom notes current products come from hyperimmunised horses and sheep, that only 10-15% of their IgGs bind venom, and that repeat vials raise adverse effects and cost). MABSTER used phage display selections together with synthetic biology and antibody/antigen engineering to find recombinant human monoclonal antibodies that are recyclable (able to neutralise more than one snake toxin per antibody) and broadly neutralising across similar toxins from several species, and it also contributed nanobodies and computationally designed minibinders that work against snake toxins in vivo, a result published in Nature and spun out as Y-king Biologics with EUR 3 million in funding. ADDovenom builds a fully synthetic platform instead, generating neutralising ADDobodies and ADDomer particles - plus nanobodies - against pathogenic snake toxins, and has shown neutralisation of recombinant PLA2 toxins and of whole venom, with Sub-Saharan Africa as the target setting in line with the WHO goal of halving snakebite mortality and morbidity by 2030. Together they show two complementary engineering routes to the same goal: re-engineering human antibody formats on one side, and a designed protein scaffold carrying many binding sites on the other.

record.text: Across the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships that set out to explain, in mice, how circuits at the front of the brain keep information alive across a short gap before it is used, what cellular mechanisms do they propose to test?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id, p.acronym, p.fundingScheme, p.startDate FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%working memory%' OR p.title ILIKE '%working memory%') AND p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Four of these fellowships propose rodent work on how prefrontal circuitry sustains information over a delay, and each names a different cellular target. StressPFCog asks whether chronic stress acts through the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) and its binding partner BRG1, a chromatin remodeler, by switching GR off either across the whole PFC or selectively in pyramidal neurons versus parvalbumin-expressing interneurons. SERWOM and PIANISM both put serotonin (5-HT) at the centre: SERWOM images pyramidal and distinct GABAergic interneuron types while mice run a delayed two alternative forced choice (2AFC) task and manipulates 5-HT release in the dorsal raphe (DR) optogenetically, while PIANISM works in acute slices, testing how 5HT receptor activity shapes the persistent firing that outlasts the initial excitatory drive through TRPC/CAN and voltage-sensitive sodium and calcium currents, in naive and chronic ketamine mice. PFCmap instead treats the architecture itself as the mechanism, using optogenetic single-cell connectivity maps to ask how recurrent networks in the superficial layers of the mouse PFC come to sustain delay-period activity as the animal matures.

MABSTER used phage display selections together with synthetic biology and antibody/antigen engineering to find recombinant human monoclonal antibodies that are recyclable (able to neutralise more than one snake toxin per antibody) and broadly neutralising across similar toxins from several species; it developed and patented a universal pH-switch for antibodies, which resulted in the spinout Y-king Biologics and EUR 3 million in secured funding, and it also contributed nanobodies and computationally designed minibinders against snake toxins, published in Nature Communications and Nature. ADDovenom builds a fully synthetic platform instead, generating neutralising ADDobodies and ADDomer particles - plus nanobodies - against pathogenic snake toxins, and has shown neutralisation of recombinant PLA2 toxins and of whole venom, with Sub-Saharan Africa as the target setting in line with the WHO goal of halving snakebite mortality and morbidity by 2030. Together they show two complementary engineering routes to the same goal: re-engineering human antibody formats on one side, and a designed protein scaffold carrying many binding sites on the other.

record.text: Which projects are developing microfluidic organ-on-chip models of the human blood-brain barrier or neurovascular unit?
record.reference_answer: About a dozen projects build microfluidic chip models of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) or the neurovascular unit (NVU), almost all justified by the failure of animal and static in vitro models to predict human drug transport into the brain. Most are dedicated BBB/NVU devices: NVU-Chip recapitulates the human NVU in a single microfluidic device and is the first to incorporate cyclic mechanical strain in a BBB model; NOVACHIP builds a scalable vessel-like BBB-on-a-chip from bioprinted endothelialized capillaries; NeuroVU adds real-time chemical and trans-endothelial electrical resistance sensing to an NVU Organ-on-Chip; SONGBIRD integrates 3D scaffolds carrying blood-brain barrier cells into a microfluidic barrier-on-chip screening platform; SweetBrain, DIANA and BrainChip4MED use NVU and brain-on-a-chip models for disease-mechanism work and for screening drugs and nanocarriers that must cross the BBB. A second group embeds a BBB compartment in a larger system: MINERVA's microbiota-gut-brain organ-on-a-chip platform, whose brain compartment hosts a complete Blood-Brain-Barrier model, and GUTVIBRATIONS' stacked gut-brain-axis organ-on-chip with a blood-brain layer. VESCEL (hiPSC-derived blood vessels in microfluidic chips, applied to blood-brain barrier function), BBBhybrid (a 1:1-scale biohybrid barriers-on-a-chip model of the brain tumour microenvironment with its blood neurovasculature) and FEBRIS (3D microfluidic devices coated with endothelial cells mimicking brain vessel networks, used to study blood-brain-barrier disruption in cerebral malaria) arrive at the same structure from vascular engineering and disease modelling.

record.reference_answer: Four of these fellowships propose mouse work on how frontal circuitry keeps information available across a delay, and each names a different mechanism to test. AG-GF trains mice on a texture discrimination task with a delay component and asks which cortical areas carry the trace, combining wide-field mapping, two-photon single-cell imaging of neurons that project top-down from frontal areas to primary somatosensory cortex, and optogenetic perturbation; it reports that during the delay persistent cortical activity sat medio-frontally in active trials. SERWOM and PIANISM both put serotonin (5-HT) at the centre: SERWOM images pyramidal and distinct GABAergic interneuron types while mice run a delayed two alternative forced choice (2AFC) task and manipulates 5-HT release in the dorsal raphe (DR) optogenetically, in a mouse model of schizophrenia, while PIANISM works in acute slices and tests how 5HT receptor activity shapes the persistent firing that outlasts the initial excitatory drive, through TRPC/CAN and voltage-sensitive sodium and calcium currents, in naive and chronic ketamine mice. PFCmap instead treats the wiring itself as the mechanism, using optogenetic single-cell connectivity maps to ask how recurrent networks in the superficial layers of the mouse PFC come to sustain delay-period activity as the animal matures.

record.text: How is European research trying to replace the traditional remedy for people bitten by poisonous snakes - the kind produced from the blood of animals repeatedly exposed to the poison - with proteins engineered in the laboratory instead?
record.reference_answer: Two projects pursue laboratory-made replacements for conventional antivenoms, which are derived from immunised animals (ADDovenom notes current products come from hyperimmunised horses and sheep, that only 10-15% of their IgGs bind venom, and that repeat vials raise adverse effects and cost). MABSTER used phage display selections together with synthetic biology and antibody/antigen engineering to find recombinant human monoclonal antibodies that are recyclable (able to neutralise more than one snake toxin per antibody) and broadly neutralising across similar toxins from several species; it developed and patented a universal pH-switch for antibodies, which resulted in the spinout Y-king Biologics and EUR 3 million in secured funding, and it also contributed nanobodies and computationally designed minibinders against snake toxins, published in Nature Communications and Nature. ADDovenom builds a fully synthetic platform instead, generating neutralising ADDobodies and ADDomer particles - plus nanobodies - against pathogenic snake toxins, and has shown neutralisation of recombinant PLA2 toxins and of whole venom, with Sub-Saharan Africa as the target setting in line with the WHO goal of halving snakebite mortality and morbidity by 2030. Together they show two complementary engineering routes to the same goal: re-engineering human antibody formats on one side, and a designed protein scaffold carrying many binding sites on the other.

Objective, verbatim: 'Snakebite envenoming is a Neglected Tropical Disease (NTD) that each year affects 2.5 million victims and kills more than 100,000, unless they are treated with antivenom. Monoclonal human antibodies with special toxin-binding properties that are sensitive towards regulation by their microenvironment (e.g. pH), which may be discovered using phage display selection, may solve this issue, providing significant societal impact by enabling the development of cost-effective antivenoms to victims in low and middle-income countries.'
Report summary, verbatim: 'In this project, phage display selections, synthetic biology, and antibody/antigen engineering techniques were harnessed in three scientific objectives in the pursuit of developing novel methodologies for the discovery of therapeutic human monoclonal antibodies that are recyclable (can neutralize more than one snake toxin per antibody), broadly neutralizing (can neutralize similar snake toxins from multiple species), and that are both broadly cross-reactive and recyclable at the same time.'

record.text: Across the Marie Sklodowska-Curie individual fellowships that set out to explain, in mice, how circuits at the front of the brain keep information alive across a short gap before it is used, what cellular mechanisms do they propose to test?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT DISTINCT p.id, p.acronym, p.fundingScheme, COALESCE(p.title,'') || ' ' || COALESCE(p.objective,'') || ' ' || COALESCE(r.teaser,'') || ' ' || COALESCE(r.summary,'') || ' ' || COALESCE(r.workPerformed,'') AS txt FROM project p LEFT JOIN report_text r ON r.projectID = p.id WHERE p.fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%') SELECT DISTINCT id, acronym, fundingScheme FROM t WHERE (txt ILIKE '%working memory%' OR txt ILIKE '%short-term memory%' OR txt ILIKE '%short term memory%' OR txt ILIKE '%delay period%' OR txt ILIKE '%memory maintenance%' OR txt ILIKE '%holding in memory%') AND (txt ILIKE '%mice%' OR txt ILIKE '% mouse %' OR txt ILIKE '%rodent%' OR txt ILIKE '% rats %') ORDER BY id

record.reference_answer: Four of these fellowships propose mouse work on how frontal circuitry keeps information available across a delay, and each names a different mechanism to test. AG-GF trains mice on a texture discrimination task with a delay component and asks which cortical areas carry the trace, combining wide-field mapping, two-photon single-cell imaging of neurons that project top-down from frontal areas to primary somatosensory cortex, and optogenetic perturbation; it reports that during the delay persistent cortical activity sat medio-frontally in active trials. SERWOM and PIANISM both put serotonin (5-HT) at the centre: SERWOM images pyramidal and distinct GABAergic interneuron types while mice run a delayed two alternative forced choice (2AFC) task and manipulates 5-HT release in the dorsal raphe (DR) optogenetically, in a mouse model of schizophrenia, while PIANISM works in acute slices and tests how 5HT receptor activity shapes the persistent firing that outlasts the initial excitatory drive, through TRPC/CAN and voltage-sensitive sodium and calcium currents, in naive and chronic ketamine mice. PFCmap instead treats the wiring itself as the mechanism, using optogenetic single-cell connectivity maps to ask how recurrent networks in the superficial layers of the mouse PFC come to sustain delay-period activity as the animal matures.
record.notes: FILTER RATIONALE: fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%' is the structured half (schema_docs lists MSCA-IF and MSCA-IF-EF-ST among the top fundingScheme values). The rest of filter_sql is an enumeration device chosen to cover the paraphrase's semantic scope in BOTH of its parts - the memory-over-a-gap sense ('working memory', 'short-term memory', 'short term memory', 'delay period', 'memory maintenance', 'holding in memory') and the mouse sense ('mice', 'mouse', 'rodent', 'rats') - searched over title, objective, teaser, summary and workPerformed rather than objective/title alone. That widening is what admits 659719 AG-GF, whose objective says 'holding in memory' and whose summary says 'short-term memory maintenance', and which the earlier objective-only device missed. At the runtime the scoped path can only build the fundingScheme half - subject matter is not a filterable column - so the topical and species parts fall to retrieval by design. ADJUDICATION (exhaustive, all 7 survivors re-read from scratch this pass): IN 659719 AG-GF - mice trained on 'texture discrimination with a delay component'; 'During the delay, in contrast, persistent cortical activity was located medio-frontally in active trials'; two-photon single-cell imaging of top-down frontal projection populations plus optogenetic perturbation. IN 888270 SERWOM - mice, 5-HT regulation of PFC GABAergic interneurons, delayed 2AFC read out during the delay period. IN 892772 PIANISM - mouse PFC slices, 5HT modulation of WM-related persistent firing. IN 898460 PFCmap - mouse PFC, optogenetic connectivity maps of the recurrent circuits that sustain delay-period activity. OUT 753296 StressPFCog - proposes how chronic stress and the glucocorticoid receptor degrade PFC-dependent cognition; 'working memory' appears once as one readout in a list ('cognitive flexibility, working memory, and novel object recognition') and no delay, maintenance or sustained-activity language appears anywhere, with the delivered GR result on reversal learning. OUT 841620 H2AH2B_Propagation - 'short-term memory' is a metaphor for fast-turnover histone marks in mouse embryonic stem cells during DNA replication; not brain, not a delay. OUT 844318 NeuroTick - mice do perform 'a complex working memory decision-making task', but the target circuit is the cerebellum, which the project's own summary calls 'a region in the back of the brain', and the aim is sensory prediction and tickling, not holding information in frontal circuits. DISCRIMINATION / FILTER LOAD-BEARING: satisfying projects outside the scheme filter - 758032 MEMCIRCUIT (ERC-STG) records from 'mice performing the same auditory working memory task' and dissects prefrontal persistent spiking with projection-specific optogenetics; 670283 SYNPRIME (ERC-ADG) is rodent synaptic work naming working memory; 949131 Hot-Coal WM (ERC-STG) is primate working memory. TEXT LOAD-BEARING: no stored column records the species used, the brain region, or the proposed cellular mechanism; all three come only from objective/report text, and the filter alone leaves 7 projects of which 3 are out. COMPLETENESS SWEEP (re-run WITHOUT the '%prefrontal%' requirement that caused the original miss): MSCA-IF projects with rodent vocabulary AND any of delayed response, delayed match, delayed non-match, persistent activity, sustained activity, persistent firing, hold/keep in mind, across a delay, delay activity, mnemonic - searched over the same five text fields, excluding the 7 survivors - returned 8 rows, all read and all out: 707084 VoidTrap (optical trapping of nanoparticles in vacuum), 708295 CA1 layers (hippocampal CA1 episodic memory), 753608 RSCHD (retrosplenial head-direction persistent activity - the nearest miss, but a posterior region and a directional compass trace rather than frontal maintenance of a stimulus), 798617 BRONC (cortical network reorganisation for behavioural switching), 840704 BrownianReactivation (modelling of hippocampal-cortical memory consolidation), 843717 Grolaries (cartilage progenitor cells), 867459 P-appetite (Drosophila feeding), 101025627 MyeSync (hippocampal CA2 myelination). TERM_STYLE: paraphrase - the question uses none of the members' distinctive vocabulary ('working memory', 'WM', 'prefrontal cortex', 'delay period', 'persistent firing', 'short-term memory'); 'front of the brain' and 'keep information alive across a short gap' are deliberate substitutions. In the scoped run over the 7 survivors, dense returned only 3 projects and all 3 are gold (898460 rank 1, 892772 rank 2, 659719 rank 3), while lexical ranks the two non-gold survivors 844318 and 841620 inside its list - so the semantic channel, not borrowed vocabulary, is what selects the gold. findings.claim: 659719 AG-GF is a defensible but materially weaker gold member than the other three. The question asks about fellowships that 'set out to explain' and what they 'propose to test'; AG-GF's proposal is a mapping study of frontal-to-somatosensory interactions in which memory is one parenthetical phase, and it proposes no cellular mechanism at all - the delay and maintenance content that qualifies it lives in the delivered report.
findings.evidence: Full text of 659719 re-read. The objective's only maintenance language is one parenthetical - 'before sensation (anticipation), during sensation (texture touch) and after sensation (holding in memory and licking for reward action)' - and its aim sentence is 'to characterize how behavior-related activity in higher-order regions (e.g. frontal area) of the mouse is spatiotemporally organized, and how does it relate to lower-order regions (e.g. somatosensory cortex)'. The proposed methods are wide-field mapping, two-photon single-cell imaging and projection labeling; no receptor, current, cell type or molecule is proposed as the mechanism, unlike 892772 PIANISM (TRPC/CAN and voltage-sensitive currents), 888270 SERWOM (5-HT receptor subtypes on distinct GABAergic cell types) or 898460 PFCmap ('circuit mechanisms that support mnemonic coding'). The delay evidence for AG-GF is all report-side. The direction of that report evidence also matters: the maintenance site is medio-frontal only on active-strategy trials and lateral-posterior on passive ones, so even the delivered result is not squarely 'frontal circuits hold the information'. record.text: Which projects build a microfluidic chip device that carries a working model of the human blood-brain barrier or neurovascular unit, either as the whole chip or as one compartment of a larger organ-on-chip system?
record.reference_answer: Thirteen projects put a working blood-brain barrier (BBB) or neurovascular unit (NVU) model inside a microfluidic chip, almost all justified by the failure of animal and static in vitro models to predict human drug transport into the brain. Most build a dedicated BBB/NVU device: NVU-Chip recapitulates the human NVU in a single microfluidic device and is the first to incorporate cyclic mechanical strain in a BBB model; NOVACHIP builds a scalable vessel-like BBB-on-a-chip from bioprinted endothelialized capillaries; NeuroVU adds real-time chemical and trans-endothelial electrical resistance sensing to an NVU Organ-on-Chip; SONGBIRD integrates 3D scaffolds carrying blood-brain barrier cells into a microfluidic barrier-on-chip screening platform; SweetBrain, DIANA and BrainChip4MED use NVU and brain-on-a-chip models for disease-mechanism work and for screening drugs and nanocarriers that must cross the BBB. Others reach the same structure from vascular or microfabrication engineering: VESCEL engineers hiPSC blood vessels in microfluidic chips and applies them on-chip to blood-brain barrier function, 3DPRINT-VASCU-CHIP's 3D-printed microfluidic devices generate and maintain living functional 3D models of the blood-brain barrier, BBBhybrid two-photon-prints a 1:1-scale biohybrid barriers-on-a-chip model of the brain tumour microenvironment with its blood neurovasculature, and FEBRIS builds 3D microfluidic devices coated with endothelial cells mimicking brain vessel networks to study blood-brain-barrier disruption in cerebral malaria. A third group carries the barrier as one compartment of a bigger chip: MINERVA's microbiota-gut-brain organ-on-a-chip platform, whose brain compartment hosts a complete Blood-Brain-Barrier model, and GUTVIBRATIONS' stacked gut-brain-axis organ-on-chip with a blood-brain layer.
record.notes: MEMBERSHIP RULE, stated in the question text so it is derivable without these notes: the project's own text must describe (i) a microfluidic or chip-based device that the project itself builds and (ii) a BBB or NVU model living in it; the device rule is by wording, and a BBB/NVU compartment inside a larger organ-on-chip system counts. Scope chosen because the corpus-wide organ-on-chip family (~60 projects by title/objective) has no enumerable boundary, while the BBB/NVU has a small set of literal names. IN (13): 101038093 NVU-Chip (3D microfluidic human NVU, first cyclic strain in a BBB model); 840626 NOVACHIP (scalable 3D BBB-on-a-chip); 832045 BBBhybrid (biohybrid barriers-on-a-chip of the brain tumour microenvironment, hCMEC/D3 endothelium + astrocytes in a microfluidic device); 757444 SONGBIRD (barrier-on-chip built around blood-brain barrier cells in a microfluidic network); 797777 NeuroVU (NVU Organ-on-Chip with sensors); 851765 SweetBrain (human-relevant NVU-OoC); 899431 DIANA (BBB-brain model Chip4D Brain on patented organ-on-chip technology); 101032481 BrainChip4MED (microfluidic brain-on-a-chip recapitulating brain tissue and BBB); 724734 MINERVA (engineered organ-on-a-chip platform whose Brain-compartment hosts a complete Blood-Brain-Barrier model - compartment clause); 953201 GUTVIBRATIONS (gut-brain-axis organ-on-chip whose deliverables include a blood-brain layer - compartment clause); 101026717 FEBRIS (3D microfluidic devices coated with endothelial cells mimicking brain vessel networks, BBB disruption in cerebral malaria); 669768 VESCEL (blood vessels engineered in microfluidic chips; report sub-aim 6 applies the blood vessels on-chip to blood-brain barrier function); 798014 3DPRINT-VASCU-CHIP (3D-printed microfluidic devices that, with hydrogel bioprinting, generate and maintain over time living functional 3D models of the blood-brain barrier). judge_decisions.rationale: All three upheld findings are the same underlying defect: the question states a topic but never states the membership rule, so neither the gold set nor the completeness sweep is derivable from the question text. As recorded, a condition that retrieves 948088 or 798014, or that reads the question as 'the chip is the project's own target', is scored as wrong for being right. The topic itself is sound and the change needed is a boundary statement plus two adjudications, not a new question.

Nothing upheld this round changes route, level, or what a system has to do to answer. The three round-1 defects are settled with verification the critic ran wider than the drafter's - a 15-term chip-free falsification arm over 19 projects that turned up no second Mal3D-BBB class - and the two members most likely to be wrong were fresh-read by the critic and hold. The three new findings all concern the accuracy of the record about individual members, and each lands on the drafter's side of the substance by the critic's own conclusion; the worst case of the sharpest of them, dropping FEBRIS, gives twelve gold and the same L3 survey cell. The question now states its own membership rule in its text, which is what round 1 was missing, and six of thirteen gold outside every top-10 is the discriminating spread an L3 survey is supposed to have, not a coverage failure, since NVU-Chip retrieves at 1/1/1/1. The remaining lexical-membership seam is visible in the question text and reproducible from the notes, so it is a disclosed property of the instrument rather than a hidden one.

why_good: The question discriminates on recall breadth at the hard end of the vector route: thirteen projects satisfy it, four conditions times ten slots surface seven of them, and six gold members (DIANA, SONGBIRD, MINERVA, GUTVIBRATIONS, FEBRIS, 3DPRINT-VASCU-CHIP) sit outside every condition's top-10, so conditions separate by how much of the set they reach rather than by whether they find the topic. It also sits inside a dense field of near-misses that the stated rule cuts cleanly: neural chips without a barrier (CONNECT, NOC, NMJ, Als-on-a-chip), tumour chips (GliomaChip, MTOAC, 3DBrainStrom), generic organ-on-chip devices (MOOAC, PTOoC, open-TOP, B-On-Chip), instrumentation for chips (BioREAD), and engineered BBB models with no chip (Mal3D-BBB, IM2PACT). Coverage axes: medical and health sciences / basic medicine, a device-and-method theme new to the bank, exact-term at L3. The label is arithmetic - |gold| = 13 - and exact-term is supported by lexical alone ranking five gold, including first.
